security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan RTL implements IOPMP HWCFG0/HWCFG2/HWCFG3 CSR registers with hardcoded bit positions matching the old v0.8 spec layout. After this spec reorganization, security-critical capability fields (chk_x, no_w, no_x, sps_en, peis, pees, mfr_en, stall_en, mdcfg_fmt, srcmd_fmt, md_entry_num) reside at entirely different register offsets and bit positions. Software linked against the reorganized spec reads HWCFG0 bit 10 expecting 'chk_x' but RTL returns old-field data at that bit; software reads new HWCFG2 bit 26 for chk_x but RTL may not implement HWCFG2 or returns unrelated data. This causes the hardware capability discovery interface to lie about which security extensions are physically present, leading secure monitor software to skip security checks that the hardware actually enforces (or conversely, to rely on checks the hardware does not perform).
security_spec.summary: HWCFG CSR field bit positions relocated across HWCFG0/HWCFG2/HWCFG3; hardcoded RTL bit mappings from v0.8 cause hardware security capability misrepresentation, enabling privilege escalation via disabled-but-believed-active protection checks
